Last month, after the TV tracking app TV Time officially shut down, its co-founder Antonio Pinto immediately announced the launch of a brand-new TV and film tracking app called Bingers, which will place greater emphasis on social features. Details are as follows.

Bingers is now available for download.

When Whip Media announced the closure of TV Time, one of its co founders immediately announced the launch of Bingers, positioning it as "a fast and beautiful wishlist paired with a fun and engaging community."

According to an exclusive report by TechCrunch, Bingers is now available for download on iOS and Android, offering a sense of continuity for users who have long been searching for an alternative — after all, TV Time was once one of the most popular TV tracking apps in the world.

Users who saved their data through TV Time's export tool before its closure can import their library into Bingers for a seamless transition; users who never exported their data, or newcomers using a TV tracking app for the first time, can build their viewing history from scratch.

Bingers significantly enhances its community-driven features, including user profiles, reviews, show ratings, GIFs, polls, and character popularity battles. Pinto told TechCrunch that these were the key elements that made TV Time so beloved by users over the years:

For users who simply want to keep track of the TV shows and movies they have watched, Bingers offers standalone wishlist and viewing history features. Similar to TV Time, the app also displays a calendar of upcoming and premiere dates, along with a countdown function showing how many days remain until each show's debut.

Bingers is now available as a free download on the App Store, and currently offers no in-app purchases.
